segments.text: This statute provides legally recognized grounds on which a Muslim woman may seek judicial dissolution of marriage in the circumstances defined by law.

The exam focus should be the purpose of the Act, statutory grounds for dissolution, procedural use, and interaction with broader Muslim family law. Exact grounds must be learned from the current official text rather than paraphrased from memory.
Primary authority: Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939, current official text on Pakistan Code/Gazette.

The Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939 is a statutory mechanism enabling a Muslim woman to seek judicial dissolution on specified grounds. It is therefore best studied as a list of legally defined grounds plus the conditions attached to them, not as a general essay on divorce.

The Act remains listed in Pakistan’s official legal database. Because the precise statutory language controls the result, students should verify the current bare Act and any applicable amendments or judicial interpretation before relying on memorized summaries.

blocks.text: How to analyse a statutory ground

segments.text: For each ground, identify: the factual condition that must exist; any minimum period stated by the statute; whether an exception or explanation applies; and what evidence could establish the condition. This converts memorization into legal reasoning.

Grounds historically associated with the Act include disappearance of the husband, failure to maintain, imprisonment, failure of marital obligations, impotence, insanity or serious disease in the statutory formulation, cruelty, and other recognized grounds. The exact wording and current legal effect should be taken from the statute rather than from a loose list.

Judicial dissolution under the 1939 Act should be distinguished from talaq and from khula as developed in Pakistani law. These routes may overlap in the practical problem of ending a marriage but rest on different legal foundations and procedures.
In a problem question, first identify the route actually invoked, then apply its own elements. Do not answer a statutory-ground question only by describing classical divorce doctrine.

items.text: The Act creates a statutory judicial route through which a Muslim woman may seek dissolution on grounds defined by law. It should therefore be studied as a rights-and-remedies statute.
Each statutory ground has its own factual conditions. In preparation, write the exact ground in one column and the facts that must be proved in another.
Judicial dissolution means the marriage is ended through a court decree on a legally recognized ground. This is conceptually different from extra-judicial modes of dissolution.
Where a question asks for application, match the wife's facts to the particular statutory ground instead of writing a general essay on divorce in Islam.

rows: Common confusion to avoid: Do not paraphrase statutory grounds so loosely that their legal conditions disappear. The operative wording should be checked from the current bare Act.

items.text: Read the current bare act and make a table of grounds.
Group grounds into absence/failure of maintenance/imprisonment/marital obligations/ill-treatment and other statutory categories only after checking exact wording.
Prepare the distinction between judicial dissolution and extra-judicial modes.

segments.text: It is a statutory route to judicial dissolution.
Each ground has legal conditions that must be proved.
Do not replace statutory wording with loose generalizations.
